column1: How much money did removing the fuel subsidy free up?
column2: About ₦15.8 trillion between June 2023 and December 2025. Most of it was shared with states and local governments.
column3: Money that once went up in smoke on petrol subsidy now funds states, councils, roads and schools.

column1: How much extra money have states and local governments received since 2023?
column2: Across all tiers, ₦26.65 trillion in additional allocations (June 2023–Dec 2025): ₦9.17tn extra to states and ₦6.66tn extra to local governments.
column3: Your governor and council chairman have more money than ever, so you can ask what they've done with it.

column1: What record did the tax service set in the first half of 2026?
column2: The Nigeria Revenue Service (formerly FIRS) collected a record ₦21.6 trillion in H1 2026.
column3: More revenue at home means less need to borrow for roads, hospitals and schools.
column5: Economy & Finance brief; Sectoral Impacts deck

column1: By how much did Customs revenue rise in 2024?
column2: To ₦6.105 trillion, up 90.4% from ₦3.206tn in 2023 and 20% above target, helped by the new B'Odogwu digital clearance platform.
column3: Plugging leaks at the ports means more money for public services. (Part of the rise reflects inflation and the exchange rate.)

column1: What did the President order in February 2026 to protect oil money?
column2: An Executive Order requiring oil and gas revenues to be paid directly into the Federation Account, scrapping NNPC's 30% management fee and the Frontier Exploration Fund deduction.
column3: More oil money now reaches the pool shared by the federal, state and local governments.

column1: What is the government's big economic target?
column2: A $1 trillion economy, set out in the Nigeria Economic Policy Framework, with tax revenue targeted at 20% of GDP.
column3: It's a clear goal voters can hold the government to.

column1: What did the Central Bank do to end the multiple exchange rates?
column2: It unified the foreign-exchange windows into one market and ended the old quasi-fiscal lending schemes, moving to orthodox monetary policy.
column3: One clear exchange rate stops a privileged few from profiting off cheap official dollars.

column1: What new protection did the CBN give bank customers against fraud?
column2: A 30-minute fraud response rule: banks must act on fraud complaints within 30 minutes.
column3: Faster action means a better chance of stopping stolen money from disappearing.

column1: How busy are Nigeria's ports now?
column2: Ports handled about 35.7 million metric tonnes of cargo in Q2 2026, up 12.3% from 31.8 million a year earlier.
column3: Busier ports mean more trade, more jobs and more revenue.
